workstream: U35 -- explicit reference-offset hook in gait.py (replaces the paused joint-offset residual direction)

background.why_this_exists: Sampled zero-mean ankle-roll RESIDUAL exploration (CaraResidualEnv, U34) was found to reliably preserve the nominal gait everywhere EXCEPT a narrow, magnitude-insensitive window at the phase-A->B weight-transfer onset, where even 0.0005 rad noise caused falls ~50-65% of the time. Per the user's own stated stop-condition ('if nominal sampled behavior is too fragile even at very small residuals, stop direct ankle-offset exploration'), that finding was treated as meeting the stop-condition, and direct ankle-offset residual learning was paused in favor of 'corrections to the teacher's balance reference or parameters.'
background.mechanism_identified: gait.py's U9 lateral roll-trim (take_step -> ss_step) latches a balance reference st['ref_ey'] = ey (CoM-to-stance-foot lateral offset, world Y axis, metres) from a SINGLE INSTANTANEOUS SAMPLE at the first controller update of phase B, then regulates dy = ey - ref_ey for the rest of the step. This single-sample latch, occurring exactly at the fragile transition previously found, is a credible mechanism for the fragility -- but source inspection alone does not establish it is the (sole) cause; that requires an intervention, per the tests below.
background.constraint: gait.py was previously treated as a hard, unmodified gate for the whole project (frozen generator/validator). That was an experimental-isolation choice, not a permanent requirement, per explicit instruction this turn -- so a minimal, explicit, EXPLICITLY OPTIONAL hook was added to gait.py itself (reference_offset_fn, default None => identical behaviour), rather than trying to reach ref_ey non-invasively (impossible: it is a plain local Python float, never crossing any boundary the existing mj_step-monkeypatch technique can intercept).

gait_py_change.diff_summary: run(config, n_steps, view, json_path, baseline_path, reference_offset_fn=None) -- new KEYWORD-ONLY-by-convention parameter, default None, so every existing positional call site (main(), _TeacherThread._run in cara_residual_env.py) is untouched and unaffected. Inside ss_step: `ref_ey_effective = st['ref_ey'] + _ref_offset_fn(st['ref_ey'])` replaces the old `dy = ey - st['ref_ey']` with `dy = ey - ref_ey_effective`. The stored latch st['ref_ey'] itself is NEVER overwritten by the offset -- kept separate per instruction, so 'offset back to zero' has an unambiguous meaning. KPA, KDA, KPH left untouched, as instructed.
gait_py_change.units_and_sign: ey = com_y - stance_foot_y (world-frame Y/lateral axis, metres), from ss_step's own definition. reference_offset_fn(ref_ey) receives the step's already-latched reference (metres, same convention) and returns an offset (metres, same convention) added to it. A positive offset raises the effective reference, which (since dy = ey - ref_ey_effective) REDUCES the trim's correction for a given +Y CoM excursion and INCREASES it for a -Y one, relative to the unmodified teacher.
gait_py_change.frozen_baseline: cara_description/scripts/gait_frozen_baseline.py -- byte-for-byte copy of gait.py immediately before this change, kept as an independent ground truth; not imported by any production path.
gait_py_change.regression_check: python3 gait.py --steps 2 after the edit: MILESTONE MET, 57mm total advance, 0.9deg final tilt, PASS/PASS -- identical to the pre-edit reference run.

test1_zero_offset_equivalence.method: Ran gait.py (default reference_offset_fn=None) and gait_frozen_baseline.py side by side, both with mujoco.mj_step monkeypatched (non-invasive, standard technique) to record qpos and ctrl at every physics substep; compared the FULL trajectory, not just endpoint metrics.
test1_zero_offset_equivalence.result: PASS -- bit-for-bit identical. 23,650 substeps compared, 19-dim qpos, max_abs_diff(qpos)=0.0, max_abs_diff(ctrl)=0.0.
test1_zero_offset_equivalence.conclusion: The hook's zero-default genuinely reproduces the pre-hook teacher exactly; the refactor introduced no behavioural change by default.

test2_causal_latch_SUPERSEDED.superseded_by: test5_latch_causality_original_failure (below) -- the velocity-kick disturbance mechanism was a different failure channel than the one actually motivating this work (the residual-noise falls), so this test's inconclusive result does not answer the question that matters; kept for the record, not as a live finding.
test2_causal_latch_SUPERSEDED.method: A one-time lateral CoM-velocity kick (data.qvel[1] += kick) applied 40ms before step_idx=0's phase-B onset (identical pre-latch state across trials, by construction of a deterministic simulation). Calibration swept kick in [0.001, 0.002, 0.004, 0.008, 0.015] m/s with reference_offset_fn recording (not altering) the resulting latch, to find a kick that both measurably biases the latch (chosen threshold: >0.5mm) AND produces a materially worse outcome, before running the actual (b)-vs-(c) causal comparison.
test2_causal_latch_SUPERSEDED.calibration_result: kick <= 0.004 m/s: latch biased by only 0.02-0.10mm, fully recovered (tilt ~4.3deg, exit_code=0, matches the ~4.4deg unperturbed baseline). kick >= 0.008 m/s: catastrophic, uncontrolled 180deg tip-over (exit_code=1) -- but the resulting latch bias at THAT kick was only 0.19-0.36mm, i.e. SMALLER than the >0.5mm threshold intended to guarantee the bias itself was large enough to matter. No tested kick magnitude produced both a large (>0.5mm) latch bias AND a merely-degraded (not already-catastrophic) outcome.
test2_causal_latch_SUPERSEDED.result: INCONCLUSIVE with this disturbance family -- reported as such, not forced to a conclusion. The intended (b) [perturbed, own latch] vs (c) [perturbed, nominal latch substituted] comparison could not be run meaningfully, because there is no intermediate kick magnitude in this sweep where the disturbance is survivable-but-degraded rather than either fully absorbed or already catastrophic.
test2_causal_latch_SUPERSEDED.interpretation_disclosed_not_overclaimed: This itself is informative: it suggests a sharp dynamic bifurcation in the underlying mechanics at this phase transition (values below ~0.005 m/s fully absorbed, values above ~0.007 m/s catastrophic, with almost no graded middle ground) rather than a graceful degradation that a 'wrong reference value' story alone would predict. This casts some doubt on whether a reference-level correction can help against a disturbance of THIS TYPE (a lateral momentum/velocity kick) at THIS phase -- the CoM trajectory may already be dynamically unrecoverable by the time any reference-based correction could act. It does NOT rule out that reference corrections could still help against smaller, more gradual disturbances, or against a different disturbance channel (e.g. a torque/moment kick, or a finer sweep between 0.004 and 0.008 m/s) -- neither has been tried.
test2_causal_latch_SUPERSEDED.not_done: A finer-grained kick sweep between 0.004 and 0.008 m/s, and/or a different disturbance channel (moment kick, longer/gentler push), which could still locate a usable intermediate regime -- flagged as a possible next micro-step, not run yet (scope discipline: this was meant to be a short probe).

test3_small_smooth_offset_probe_SUPERSED.superseded_by: test4_phase_indexed_pulse_test (below) -- this test used a SUSTAINED (whole-step) offset on only one leg, exactly the confound pattern flagged in explicit_flag_not_yet_isolated below; the brief, phase-indexed, both-legs redesign resolved it. Kept for the record, not as a live finding.
test3_small_smooth_offset_probe_SUPERSED.method: On the fully UNPERTURBED nominal run (no kick), a constant reference_offset was smoothly ramped on (0.4s smoothstep) at the start of step_idx=0's phase B, held through phases B+C+D, and ramped back to exactly zero before phase E (transfer) -- magnitudes chosen (0.2/0.5/1.0mm) so that KPA*offset stays within the ~0.05 rad envelope probe_phase_pulse.py (U34/U35 prep) already established as bidirectionally safe for direct ankle-roll JOINT residual pulses -- an earlier attempt at 2/5/10mm (implying 0.1-0.5 rad corrections) was a scale-calibration miss, not a hook finding, and is superseded by these numbers.
test3_small_smooth_offset_probe_SUPERSED.internal_consistency_check: For every SAFE trial, the recorded delta_ctrl on r_ankle_roll matched the trim law's own algebra (delta_ctrl = -sfn*KPA*offset) to within numerical noise (max_err 0.03-0.06, vs. control magnitudes ~0.1-1.0). This confirms the hook is wired correctly and doing exactly what the formula says -- it is not a bug in the mechanism. For every FAILING trial the check breaks down badly (max_err ~10-22), consistent with the robot having already inverted (state saturated, the small-perturbation algebra no longer applies), not with a hook malfunction.

result.negative_offsets (-0.2, -0.5, -1.0 mm): ALL SAFE. tilt ~4.4deg (matches baseline's 4.39deg closely), exit_code=0, touchdown continues normally after step 0.
result.positive_offsets (+0.2, +0.5, +1.0 mm): ALL FAIL. Every magnitude, including the smallest tested (+0.2mm, implying just a 0.01 rad ctrl correction), produces a catastrophic, uncontrolled 180deg tip-over on the completely UNDISTURBED nominal walk.

test3_small_smooth_offset_probe_SUPERSED.explicit_flag_not_yet_isolated: This sign-dependent asymmetry closely parallels the EARLIER ankle-roll joint-offset asymmetry (U34's probe_residual_bound.py: constant -0.001 rad failed, +0.005 rad survived) that turned out to be a whole-episode/sustained-bias CONFOUND, not a fundamental sign-sensitivity -- resolved only once brief, phase-indexed, per-leg pulses (probe_phase_pulse.py) showed clean bidirectional symmetry. The SAME confounds are present here and have NOT yet been ruled out: (1) only ONE stance leg/step (r_ankle_roll, step_idx=0, lead=l_) was tested -- the other leg/step (l_ankle_roll, step_idx=1) has not; (2) the offset was SUSTAINED across nearly the whole step (B+C+D, ~6000 controller updates), not a BRIEF pulse like the joint-space probes that established symmetry; (3) the natural drift direction of ey during this specific step/stance was not independently characterized, so it is not yet known whether '+offset' happens to ask the trim to tolerate MORE of whatever direction the CoM is already drifting toward (plausibly destabilizing by construction) versus a leg/topology-specific sign effect. Per the lesson already learned twice in this project (U27, U34->U35), this asymmetry is reported as REAL AND MEASURED, but NOT YET CONCLUDED to be a fundamental property of positive reference offsets in general.
test3_small_smooth_offset_probe_SUPERSED.recommended_next_micro_step_not_yet_run: Repeat this exact probe as a BRIEF, phase-indexed pulse (ramp on/off within ~0.5-1s, not sustained across the whole step) on BOTH stance legs (r_ankle_roll/step_idx=0 AND l_ankle_roll/step_idx=1), matching the design that successfully disambiguated the earlier joint-offset case.

test4_phase_indexed_pulse_test.purpose: Answers ONLY 'does the interface offer usable, bidirectional correction authority at the phases a learned corrector would need it', with NO external disturbance -- deliberately separated from latch causality (test5), which they answer independently.
test4_phase_indexed_pulse_test.design: Bounded 12-case comparison: 2 stance legs (step_idx=0/stance=r_, step_idx=1/stance=l_) x 3 timings (early single support ~0.2s after liftoff, mid single support = middle of swing, before touchdown ~0.2s before place) x 2 signs (+-0.2mm world-Y, amplitude NOT expanded beyond this). Each pulse: smoothstep on/hold/off, ~0.2s total, fixed width -- NOT amplitude-graded. Every case ran through the REST of the walk (not just the pulse window). toward/away labelled from data (sign of offset vs. sign of that leg's own baseline latch, not assumed a priori): step0/r_ latches at ref_ey=+13.821mm, step1/l_ at ref_ey=-14.987mm (confirms the natural latch sign flips between legs, as expected from geometry).
test4_phase_indexed_pulse_test.result: 10/12 SAFE: tracking error stayed ~2.4-2.7mm (essentially the pulse's own magnitude scaled through the trim law, not amplified), no actuator force/ctrl saturation, contact-force deltas under 20N, no 40deg exceedance. 2/12 FAILED, both at the EARLY timing, both at the SAME RAW WORLD-Y SIGN (+0.2mm) -- step0/r_ early +0.2mm ('away' label) and step1/l_ early +0.2mm ('toward' label). Because the SAME raw sign fails on both legs despite opposite toward/away labels, the danger is NOT explained by the toward/away framing itself -- something tied to world direction specifically at the early-single-support instant is responsible, not a leg-symmetric toward/away effect. This is a real, deterministic, reproducible finding (no noise/stochasticity involved -- single deterministic run per case), not a confound of the kind found in the now-superseded test3.
test4_phase_indexed_pulse_test.caveat: In the 2 failing cases, reported peak_reference_error_mm and peak_delta_ctrl values are contaminated by post-40deg-collapse dynamics (e.g. peak_dy=189mm, delta_ctrl=10.57rad -- physically meaningless once the robot has already inverted, per the FALL_TILT_DEG=40deg convention adopted this turn). The 40deg-exceeded flag and its timestamp are the meaningful outputs for those 2 cases, not the peak magnitudes.
test4_phase_indexed_pulse_test.conclusion: The reference-offset interface itself is NOT generally fragile: at +-0.2mm it is safe, symmetric, and non-saturating in 10 of 12 tested phase/leg/sign combinations, with negligible tracking error. It has one narrow, direction-specific failure mode confined to the early-single-support instant (near the latch) -- consistent with, and likely the same underlying mechanism as, the previously-found ankle-residual fragility at that same transition.

test5_latch_causality_original_failure.purpose: Revisits latch causality using an ORIGINAL residual-noise failure (the actual motivating problem) instead of a new external kick, per instruction that the kick was a different disturbance mechanism.
test5_latch_causality_original_failure.method: Found seed=4000 (std=0.0005 rad ankle-space Gaussian residual noise, same mechanism as the original truncated-window sweep) reproducibly falls at decision 300 (6.00s), tilt 43.62deg. Two matched runs from that seed: Run A (normal latch) vs. Run B (identical residual draws, but reference_offset_fn forces the step's effective reference to the UNDISTURBED zero-residual run's own latch value, ref_ey_nominal=+13.821mm, for the whole step). Verified bit-for-bit identical through decision 275 (pre-latch and the latch instant itself) before the two runs are allowed to diverge -- confirms 'everything before the intervention matches, including the teacher's internal state' rather than assuming it.
test5_latch_causality_original_failure.result: BOTH FAIL, within 2 decisions of each other (Run A: decision 300, tilt 43.62deg; Run B: decision 302, tilt 44.91deg). Per the specified outcome rules: 'if both fail, latch correction alone is insufficient.'
test5_latch_causality_original_failure.conclusion: The biased latch is NOT the (sole, or even a materially rescuing) cause of this specific residual-noise failure. Even the MOST GENEROUS possible reference-based intervention (forcibly substituting the exact undisturbed reference value) does not prevent it. The failure's root cause lies elsewhere in the physical state the residual noise has already produced by that point (e.g. joint/CoM velocities, momentum, or contact state divergent from nominal) -- something a reference-value correction cannot reach, regardless of how it is computed or learned.

kick_implementation_clarification.instruction: Clarify the kick implementation before drawing conclusions from it: changing floating-base lateral velocity is not generally identical to prescribing whole-body CoM velocity. Record the actual velocity change achieved.
kick_implementation_clarification.CORRECTED_after_external_review: The FIRST attempt at this measurement (data.subtree_com read immediately before/after mj_step) was itself wrong, per external code review: MuJoCo's mj_step computes derived kinematic quantities (subtree_com included) from the qpos AS OF THE START of that call (mj_fwdPosition), THEN integrates qpos/qvel forward (mj_step2/Euler) -- so data.subtree_com read right after mj_step returns still reflects the PRE-integration configuration. A finite difference across mj_step calls this way measures motion preceding the kick, not its effect, and produced a spurious ~0.03mm/s figure with no evidential value.
kick_implementation_clarification.corrected_method: Instantaneous v_com = J_com(q).qdot via mj_jacSubtreeCom(model, data, jacp, 0), evaluated at the SAME q immediately before and after modifying qvel[1] -- no physics advanced between the two evaluations. mj_kinematics + mj_comPos are called explicitly first to refresh xpos/subtree_com for the qpos currently in data (these too lag qpos by one mj_step call otherwise), so the Jacobian is evaluated at a configuration consistent with the qvel it is dotted against.
kick_implementation_clarification.corrected_measurement: For the representative kick (data.qvel[1] += 0.008 m/s, applied at substep 2730): qvel1_delta = 0.008000 m/s (exact, as expected). v_com_y_delta = 0.008000 m/s -- matching the requested kick almost exactly, not the ~0.03mm/s the buggy method reported.
kick_implementation_clarification.conclusion: REVERSES the earlier claim. At this instant (quasi-static gait, joint velocities near zero), a floating-base linear-qvel kick DOES transfer essentially fully to whole-body CoM velocity -- the two are not generally identical in principle (the caveat that prompted this check is correct as a general statement), but in THIS specific case they coincide almost exactly. The now-superseded test2's kick magnitudes (0.001-0.03 m/s) should therefore be read as genuine CoM-velocity-scale disturbances of that size, not the negligible effect originally (and wrongly) reported. This does not change test2's SUPERSEDED status (it was superseded because the disturbance mechanism didn't match the motivating problem, not because of this specific bug) or test5's core finding (unaffected -- see below), but it does correct a factual misstatement made earlier in this workstream.

external_code_review_2026-09-17_ROUND_2.summary: A second external review (source-only, scheduling functions executed in isolation, no MuJoCo run) found 3 further concrete defects, all confirmed by direct re-read of the actual code before acting.
external_code_review_2026-09-17_ROUND_2.finding_1_step1_pulses_actually_hit_step: CONFIRMED, REAL, SERIOUS. make_offset_fn()'s counter increments on EVERY ss_step call across the WHOLE gait.run() call (not reset per step), but the pulse center passed to it was a step-LOCAL value (0-6200 range) with no step_idx*calls_per_step offset. Since step 0's ss_step calls occupy global counter positions [0, 6200) and step 1's occupy [6200, 12400), every 'step 1' case's pulse (centered at a local value like 100/3000/5900) actually fired during STEP 0's calls, not step 1's -- meaning all 6 test4_phase_indexed_pulse_test 'step1/l_' results were invalid: they perturbed step 0 again and then merely observed a longer subsequent walk. This directly invalidates the earlier claim that 'the same raw world-Y sign fails on both legs' -- that was never evidence about two different legs.
external_code_review_2026-09-17_ROUND_2.finding_2_dy_computation_also_misaligned: CONFIRMED, REAL. analyze_case's case_rows correctly selected step_idx's own rows, but indexed offset_trace (which is GLOBAL, indexed from the whole run's start) as offset_trace[0:len(case_rows)] unconditionally -- correct only for step_idx=0 (where the global and local indexing coincide), silently wrong for step_idx=1 (paired step 1's ey values against step 0's offset samples).
external_code_review_2026-09-17_ROUND_2.finding_3_missing_error_outcome: CONFIRMED, REAL, in cara_residual_env.py's _TeacherThread._run(): outcome is pre-initialized to ('done', None) and only overwritten in the _Fell/_Stopped except clauses; any OTHER exception from gait.run() (e.g. a bug in a caller-supplied reference_offset_fn) would propagate past an uncaught path, but the finally block still sends the stale ('done', None) BEFORE that exception surfaces -- the caller would see an ordinary episode completion instead of a crash. Confirmed this does NOT explain any reported fall (_Fell is handled explicitly, and all latch-causality runs used _Fell-based termination) -- a correctness gap found before it caused a real misdiagnosis, not evidence that one occurred.
fixes_applied: u35_phase_indexed_reference_pulses.py: pulse center now computed as step_idx*calls['per_step'] + timing_center(...); analyze_case slices offset_trace from the correct step-local start (case_offsets = offset_trace[start:start+len(case_rows)]); added an explicit placement assertion (every nonzero offset sample must fall within the intended step's own call range) and an explicit pre-intervention bit-exact check (trial qpos must match baseline qpos up to the pulse's own first nonzero sample) -- both now REPORTED per case (pre_intervention_bitexact, first_pulse_substep), not just assumed.

u35_phase_indexed_reference_pulses.py: peak-error/command-delta/saturation/contact summaries now CUT at the first 40deg exceedance (post-failure motion no longer contaminates the primary summary fields); the full, uncut values are retained separately as *_full_incl_postfail fields, not discarded.

cara_residual_env.py: added _TeacherError wrapper and a broad `except Exception` in _run() that sends ('error', _TeacherError(e)) instead of falling through to the stale ('done', None); reset()/step() now raise the original exception immediately on receiving msg=='error'.

cara_residual_env.py: documented (module docstring) that the module-level mujoco.mj_step monkeypatch permits only ONE active _TeacherThread/CaraResidualEnv per process -- a real, disclosed structural limitation of the technique, not enforced at runtime; every script in this project already satisfies it (one env at a time, closed before the next).
external_code_review_2026-09-17_ROUND_2.rerun_result: Reran the full corrected 12-case pulse test (all 12, not just the 6 step_idx=1 cases, since step_idx=0's ORIGINAL indexing coincided with the fix and required no correction, but the new cut-at-failure/placement-assertion logic applies uniformly and no raw per-case traces had been persisted to recompute from). Every case now reports placed_ok=true (pre-intervention bit-exact, placement assertion passed) -- the fix is confirmed working, not just theorized.
external_code_review_2026-09-17_ROUND_2.corrected_12case_result: 1/12 cases now exceed 40deg (down from the previously-reported, partially-invalid 2/12): step0/r_ early +0.2mm ('away') still fails at t=13.21s, UNCHANGED from before (this case's placement was never affected by the bug, since step_idx=0 needs zero offset). ALL 6 step1/l_ cases now SURVIVE, including BOTH signs at the early timing (peak_dy ~2.5mm, d_ctrl ~0.02rad, no saturation, no fall) -- a materially different result from the original (mis-scheduled) run, which had reported step1/l_ early +0.2mm as a failure.
external_code_review_2026-09-17_ROUND_2.retraction: The earlier claim 'the danger is not explained by toward/away -- something tied to world direction specifically at the early-single-support instant is responsible, not a leg-symmetric toward/away effect' is RETRACTED. It was built on a comparison between step0's genuine early/away failure and step1's spurious (mis-scheduled, actually-step-0) 'failure' -- not two independent legs. The corrected data shows NO analogous fragility on step1/l_'s own early window in EITHER sign. The remaining single failure (step0/r_, early, +0.2mm/away) is not yet shown to generalize to the other leg, to a world-direction principle, or to anything beyond this one specific (leg, timing, sign) combination -- it is real, reproducible, and unexplained, not a general property of early-single-support pulses.
external_code_review_2026-09-17_ROUND_2.net_effect_on_headline_finding: If anything, the corrected result is a SLIGHTLY STRONGER version of 'the interface is not generally fragile' (11/12 safe vs. the previously reported 10/12) -- but the specific characterization of WHERE the one exception lives, and what it means, has changed and is now narrower and less understood than previously stated. Per instruction, neither of the two clean decision-rule branches ('tiny early pulses still cause falls' vs. 'correctly placed pulses survive') fires cleanly: step0/r_'s early/away pulse still fails, but step1/l_'s early pulses (both signs) do not -- a mixed, leg/sign-specific result requiring more localized investigation before a controller-design decision, not a global verdict either way.

external_code_review_2026-09-17.summary: An external source review (no ability to execute the code) found 5 concrete measurement/metric defects. Each was independently verified against the actual current source before acting. Two were real bugs in LIVE (still-relied-upon) code and were fixed and rerun; three were real but confined to already-superseded diagnostics or to gait.py's own pre-existing (unmodified by this workstream) internal reporting.
external_code_review_2026-09-17.finding_1_kick_com_velocity_wrong: CONFIRMED, REAL, was in live code (u35_latch_causality.py's addendum). Fixed via mj_jacSubtreeCom (see kick_implementation_clarification above) and rerun. Reverses the earlier ~0.03mm/s claim to a corrected ~0.008 m/s (matching the kick almost exactly).
external_code_review_2026-09-17.finding_2_tracking_error_is_abs_ey_not_d: CONFIRMED, REAL, but confined to the already-SUPERSEDED test3_small_smooth_offset_probe (`tracking_dy_peak_mm` field used `max(abs(r['ey']))`, not `ey - ref_ey_effective`). Verified test4_phase_indexed_pulse_test's `peak_reference_error_mm` already computes the correct dy = ey - (ref_ey_baseline + offset) -- confirmed by direct re-read of u35_phase_indexed_reference_pulses.py's analyze_case(). Does not affect any live conclusion.
external_code_review_2026-09-17.finding_3_trim_law_check_misaligned: CONFIRMED, REAL, exact mechanism as described (offset_trace indexed from phase-B onset; delta_ctrl_full indexed from simulation start; a naive [:n] slice does not align them) -- but again confined to the SUPERSEDED test3's trim-law consistency check, which is retracted (its claimed 'PASS' was not a valid verification). test4 does not attempt any trim-law identity check at all -- its peak_delta_ctrl_* fields are honestly-labeled rollout differences (trial ctrl minus baseline ctrl, correctly substep-aligned via each row's own recorded absolute substep index, not a naive positional slice) and were never used to claim algebra verification. General principle accepted: verifying a LOCAL control-law identity requires evaluating both commands at the same state/history without advancing physics; a rollout diff conflates the direct effect with everything the offset changes about subsequent dynamics. No live check currently claims to verify the trim law's algebra; none is planned unless specifically needed.
external_code_review_2026-09-17.finding_4_native_milestone_omits_phaseB: CONFIRMED, REAL, verified by direct re-read of gait.py: ss_step(..., record=False) (used throughout phase B's lift ramp and phase D's 0.4s post-place hold) returns before updating M['tilt'/'margin'/'slip'/'sat'/'stance_corners']; phases A and E never call ss_step at all. gait.py's own 'MILESTONE MET' / PASS verdict and M-based safety metrics therefore only ever reflect phases C and D's ramp, not the whole step -- a genuine, pre-existing gap in gait.py's own reporting (not introduced by this workstream, and not something this workstream is modifying gait.py's internals to fix, per instruction to make only the minimal reference-offset hook change). Every pass/fail verdict actually relied upon in this workstream (tests 1, 4, 5) came from independent external tilt tracking computed directly from the full qpos trace every substep, never from gait.py's internal M dict -- so this gap does not undermine those results. It DOES mean the 'regression check: MILESTONE MET' statements made when confirming gait.py's edit didn't change default behavior only guarantee agreement on the portions M actually covers (C, D-ramp) plus the fully-independent bit-exact qpos/ctrl trace comparison (test1), which is unaffected by M's gap since it compares raw state, not M's summary.
external_code_review_2026-09-17.finding_5_contact_force_max_not_sum: CONFIRMED, REAL, in shared run_recorded() (u35_reference_hook_verify.py): contact_force_n took max() across simultaneous stance-foot/floor contact points instead of summing them, undercounting total load whenever more than one contact point is active. FIXED (now sums). This affects test4's peak_contact_force_delta_n values, which were computed with the buggy version and are NOT re-run this turn -- per instruction to rerun only the nominal-reference/seed-4000 pair (test5), test4's contact-force numbers are marked unreliable pending a future rerun, not retracted from the qualitative 10/12-safe finding (which did not depend on the exact contact-force magnitude, only on the 40deg tilt threshold and actuator-saturation flags, both computed independently of this bug). The 'touch_after_step0 checks EITHER foot' critique in the same finding applies to the superseded test3, which had that field; test4 never included a touch/contact boolean field.
external_code_review_2026-09-17.test5_core_result_unaffected: The main Run-A-vs-Run-B comparison and its 'both fail' conclusion do not depend on any of the 5 findings (they use CaraResidualEnv's own external tilt-based _Fell, and a raw qpos-trace bit-diff) -- reconfirmed identical after the fix: Run A fell at decision 300 (43.62deg), Run B at decision 302 (44.91deg), pre-latch decision-level diff = 0.0. final_decision.rules_given: usable brief reference corrections -> retain interface + calibrate disturbance-learning task; latch substitution consistently rescues failures -> consider a deterministic latch fix before RL; even brief corrections remain extremely fragile -> stop residual training on this interface and review the teacher's transition robustness directly.
final_decision.which_applies_SUPERSEDED: The '10/12 safe... one narrow direction-specific exception' characterization below is RETRACTED per external_code_review_2026-09-17_ROUND_2 -- it was built partly on a mis-scheduled test (step1/l_'s pulses actually re-perturbed step 0). See which_applies_CORRECTED for the current basis.
final_decision.which_applies: [SUPERSEDED -- kept for the record, not as a live finding] A hybrid not cleanly covered by exactly one bin, resolved as follows. Test4 rules out bin 3's PREMISE: brief reference corrections are NOT generally/extremely fragile (10/12 safe, small and predictable effect, one narrow direction-specific exception at the early-single-support instant). Test5 rules out bin 1 and bin 2's PREMISE for the motivating problem: even the single strongest possible reference-based intervention (exact nominal-latch substitution) fails to rescue the actual residual-noise failure it was meant to test, so calibrating a disturbance-learning task on this channel, or building a deterministic latch fix, would both be investing in a lever already shown insufficient for the problem that motivated this whole workstream.
final_decision.which_applies_CORRECTED: Test4's corrected result (11/12 safe, one failure isolated to step0/r_/early/away, NOT replicated on step1/l_'s early window in either sign) still rules out bin 3's premise -- if anything more clearly than before, since the failure count went down and the earlier 'affects both legs' claim (which would have suggested something more structural) is retracted. Test5's finding is unaffected by either round of review (it never depended on ey/dy/contact computations) and still rules out bin 1/2's premise exactly as before: even exact nominal-latch substitution fails to rescue the actual residual-noise failure. Per the second reviewer's own framing, this is now a MIXED result requiring localized investigation, not a clean two-branch outcome: correctly-placed pulses mostly survive (supports treating the interface as usable), but one specific, reproducible, still-unexplained failure remains at step0/r_'s early-support/away-direction case -- not yet shown to be a leg-symmetric or world-direction effect, not yet ruled out as something else entirely.
final_decision.decision: UNCHANGED in substance, restated on the corrected evidence: STOP treating reference-level correction as the fix for the phase-B fragility mechanism motivating this workstream (test5's finding, unaffected by either review round, already settles this). Do NOT proceed to calibrate the disturbance-learning task, build a residual policy, or run PPO on this interface for that purpose. Additionally, per the corrected test4 result: the remaining step0/r_/early/away failure is an open, localized question (not a global 'early single support is fragile' finding) -- establishing whether it is leg-specific, sign-specific, or an artifact of this one test setup is a prerequisite before any further controller-design decision that touches that specific window, per the second review's explicit framing ('establish which leg was actually perturbed before making another controller-design decision').
final_decision.not_done: No disturbance calibration, no training-mixture design, no residual-policy architecture, no PPO, and (per the second review's explicit instruction) no new parameter sweep -- only the bounded correction-and-rerun of the existing 12-case test and the existing nominal-reference/seed-4000 pair.
